prompt: Build a MoneyAmount value type that stores an exact number of cents, normalises whatever dollars-and-cents pair it is handed, and formats negatives as "-$1.50".
explanation: Money must never be held in a double, because values like 0.10 cannot be represented exactly and the errors accumulate across arithmetic. Storing one long cent total makes every operation exact integer arithmetic, and the dollars/cents split is recovered on demand with / 100 and % 100. Taking Math.abs before splitting keeps the parts positive so the sign can be printed once at the front instead of leaking into the cents.
hints: Keep a single private long field holding the total in cents; of(dollars, cents) is just dollars * 100 + cents.
dollarsPart and centsPart should work on Math.abs(totalCents) so that a negative amount still reports 1 and 50 rather than -1 and -50.
Build toString from a sign prefix plus String.format(java.util.Locale.US, "$%d.%02d", ...) so that five cents prints as $0.05.
